summary: Key-based identity and QR v2. Host id = sha256(SPKI) (computed via the rustls ring key provider from the private key; rustls refuses a cert whose SPKI differs), so HostIdentity::rotate_certificate keeps every pin, the registry binding and all proofs. Legacy state migrates: a device registry bound to the v1 certificate pin is re-bound to the host id of the same key on host start (DeviceRegistry::migrate_legacy_host; any other mismatch still fails closed). QR v2 `zenpi://pair?v=2&host_id=..&hints=lan:IP:PORT[,tailnet:IP:PORT..]&token=..&expires=..` carries 1..4 ordered, distinct hints that are issued/refreshed/retired with the one-use token (InviteIssuer::issue_hints); v1 still parses strictly; v1/v2 field sets never mix. Android: PinnedTrustManager accepts the host-id pin (rotation-proof) or a v1 cert pin and records both names of the verified cert; challenge must name the verified cert and proofs sign that name; PairingInvite parses v1/v2 with hints; saved hosts carry a pin kind and v1-pinned hosts are re-pinned to the host id after one pinned TLS handshake on the next foreground refresh (PairedHostStore.migratePin), keeping display, cursors and pending requests.

notes: 'Token-bound hints' is implemented as: hints are part of the one active invite record, issued, refreshed (refresh re-issues the same hints with a new token) and retired with the token; Pair admission only succeeds for the active token. Hints are not added to the device pairing signature (no proof-format change); they are routing advice only and the pin is checked on every path.
PairingInvite keeps `address` (= hints[0].address) and `fingerprint` (v2: host id, v1: cert pin) to avoid churn in many callers; validate_at enforces the consistency.

HostIdentity::rotate_certificate exists for the rotation proof (tests); no CLI rotates certificates (rcgen certs are valid until 4096). HostIdentity::legacy_fingerprint is used only for registry migration.

Legacy (v1-pinned) saved hosts keep working before migration: HostClient accepts the challenge naming either the key id or the cert hash of the TLS-verified certificate, so an older host binary that still names itself by cert hash also works.
host-key-rotation.json is fixture-only data (includes a test-only private key) generated once from HostIdentity::load_or_create + rotate_certificate; Rust re-verifies it on load.
